title: Orchestrated latency bursts and GPU-pool pressure experiment
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Objective: Validate end-to-end behavior of Redwood inference under combined failure modes: simulated region network partition (partial region loss), progressive GPU pool exhaustion on a serving pool, and dependency blackholes (datastore and auth proxy). We will measure SLO adherence, circuit-breaker tripping thresholds, observed failover latency between regions, and effectiveness of tiered load-shedding policies. The experiment will be conducted against a dedicated staging namespace that mirrors production traffic patterns (mix: 70% short-generation, 20% streaming chat, 10% embeddings) and runs during a guarded test window with on-call and SEV rollback plan in place. Success criteria: SLO metrics match predicted degradation curves and automatic fallbacks keep 99% of high-priority requests within the P99 target for the primary region, or failover to secondary region within the documented RTO; circuit breakers trip without cascading failures; load-shedding preserves prioritized traffic (control plane and high-priority API keys) while shedding lower-priority work.
acceptance_criteria: Can induce partial region network partition in staging that causes cross-region RPCs to experience >500ms median latency within 5 minutes
Simulate GPU pool exhaustion such that 80% of new inference requests in the affected pool receive either queued/dropped responses or are redirected within configured SLA windows
Circuit breaker metrics and logs show tripping at configured thresholds (error rate 5% over 1m or latency 2x SLO) and recovery after backoff policies
Failover path: automated router policy sends traffic to secondary region within 30s and ramp to 100% in 180s with no data corruption
Load-shedding policy maintains 95% success for high-priority keys and drops <=30% of low-priority, measured per-minute during peak
No untested config pushed to production; all changes restricted to staging tenants and RBAC gates enabled
test_plan: Precheck: snapshot current staging config, confirm telemetry ingestion to canary dashboards (cost and latency), and notify oncall
Phase 1 (Baseline): run 2h of replayed production traffic and record SLO baselines for short/stream/embeddings
Phase 2 (Dependency Blackhole): inject blackhole for datastore calls in region-east-1 for 15min and observe graceful degradation and circuit breaker behavior
Phase 3 (GPU Pressure): create synthetic load to exhaust 70-90% of the GPU pool for pool-A via synthetic clients that open long-running streams and pinned KV-cache requests
Phase 4 (Combined): run dependency blackhole + GPU pressure concurrently and trigger a controlled partial network partition to simulate region-level API egress saturation

Phase 5 (Failover & Recovery): validate router policy sends traffic to secondary region, verify KV cache warmup behavior and request routing, and then stepwise remove injections to confirm recovery and auto-heal
Post-run: collect traces, token-level cost, and model outputs for sample requests to detect regression in quality or truncation anomalies
runbook_changes: Add 'chaos.gpu_pool_pressure' playbook section to the oncall runbook with exact mitigation steps and abort criteria
Document new circuit-breaker debug commands and log filters (kafka topic names and trace ids)
Add a one-click rollback to routing policy for immediate cutback to global-safe mode
monitoring_deltas: Add P99 and error-rate heatmaps per region and per-priority key in Console->SLOs
Emit new metric 'chaos.experiment.active' with labels experiment_id and stage
Create alert threshold: >10% of requests diverted for >2m triggers SEV-1 to oncall
Add cost anomaly watch for synthetic load runs to avoid runaway billing
related_incidents: INC-2026-01-region-blip - recent failover tear down in us-west-2
notes: Trade-offs discussed: aggressive failover reduces tail-latency but increases cross-region egress cost; decided to validate both cost and latency curves during the experiment. We will not push any routing fallback to production without a separate release and exec sponsor signoff.
risks: Synthetic load may contaminate shared metrics if not properly labeled; ensure metric tags include experiment_id=ENG-12890
Cache warming on the secondary region may lead to short-lived elevated latency for warmup period
Unexpected interactions with Dedicated customer namespaces if staging configs leak — RBAC gates must be enforced
mitigations: Run in isolated staging projects with quota limits and cost caps
Throttle synthetic clients using adaptive rampers and automated abort on alert
Pre-approve experiment with Security and Platform leads and include a rollback window
